evaluation.strategy: Book a last-minute flight from Denver tonight or early Friday morning to Seattle (SEA). Remote work is the play for Thursday (today) as high winds and downed trees on Highway 410 will likely cause lift and road delays. Commit a full PTO day for Friday, March 13, to target the reopening of White Pass or the first true opening of Crystal’s high-alpine bowls. Depart Saturday morning to avoid the 2-hour lines typical of a post-storm weekend in the Cascades.
evaluation.snow_quality: Expect a classic 'Cascade Cream' transition. Thursday's initial loading is dense (SLR 7:1 to 8:1), which acts as the perfect 'glue' to bury the low-tide subsurface. Friday's 20-inch pulse stacks higher-quality, supportable powder on top as temperatures drop into the low 20s, providing a surfy, bottomless feel.
evaluation.crowd_estimate: Friday is your window for untouched powder. While the 70-inch headline will draw every skier in Seattle, the mid-week timing of the biggest dump preserves longevity. White Pass offers the best snow-to-crowd ratio; being ignored by the mega-pass crowds and reopening after a closure means powder will last all day Friday. Avoid Saturday at all costs as regional surges will track the mountain out by 10:30 AM.
evaluation.closure_risk: High road closure risk on Highway 410 for avalanche control today and tomorrow morning; staying in Greenwater or Packwood is a critical tactical move to ensure you are inside the gates when the road opens.
